purpose: What a review panel checks in a new search analysis before it accepts the strategy, the background estimate, the validation, the sensitivity and the note. Each item states the evidence that satisfies it and what counts as a blocking finding. Items with a rule are computed by review_rubric.evaluate over the review packet the analysis declares; items without a rule are judgment items the reviewer answers with located evidence. A run may tighten this rubric with a pinned overlay; an overlay adds items or strengthens them and never removes one.

items.question: Is every signal region motivated by the kinematics of the signal it targets?
items.evidence: Each signal region names the signal kinematics that motivate its selection.
items.blocking: A signal region is declared without a motivation, or no signal region is declared.

items.question: Is the blinding policy stated?
items.evidence: A statement of which regions are blinded and when they are unblinded.
items.blocking: The analysis states no blinding policy.

items.question: When no observed data enter the result, is the construction of the pseudo-data stated?
items.evidence: A declaration of whether observed data are used and, when they are not, how the pseudo-data are built.
items.blocking: The use of observed data is not declared, or a result without observed data does not state its pseudo-data.

items.question: Was the selection optimised on expected quantities only, without the observed signal-region data?
items.evidence: Located evidence of the optimisation inputs.
items.blocking: The selection was tuned on observed signal-region data.

items.question: Does every major background have a control region or a cited estimation method?
items.evidence: Each major background names at least one control region or cites the method that estimates it.
items.blocking: A major background has neither a control region nor a cited method, or no major background is declared.

items.question: Is every fitted normalisation factor reported with its uncertainty?
items.evidence: The list of normalisation factors, each with its process, value and uncertainty.
items.blocking: The normalisation factors are not declared, or one is reported without its value or uncertainty.

items.question: Is the signal contamination of every control region quantified?
items.evidence: Each control region reports its largest signal fraction over the signal points studied.
items.blocking: The control regions are not declared, or one has no quantified signal contamination.

items.question: Is the multijet background estimated by a data-driven or simulation-based method with a closure test, or shown to be negligible?
items.evidence: The multijet method and its closure result, or the justification for neglecting the background.
items.blocking: The multijet background has no method with a closure result and no justification for neglecting it.

items.question: Is the background model compared with the data or pseudo-data in validation regions after the fit?
items.evidence: Each validation region reports its post-fit comparison.
items.blocking: A validation region has no post-fit comparison, or no validation region is declared.

items.question: Does every data-driven background estimate carry a closure test?
items.evidence: Each background estimated from data reports the result of its closure test.
items.blocking: A data-driven estimate has no closure test.

items.question: Do heavily weighted simulated samples report their effective event count and an adequacy assessment in the regions they populate?
items.evidence: Each heavily weighted sample reports its effective event count and the assessment that it is adequate.
items.blocking: The simulated samples are not declared, or a heavily weighted sample has no effective count or adequacy assessment.

items.question: When a multivariate method is used, are the folds assigned by the event identifier?
items.evidence: A declaration of whether a multivariate method is used and, when it is, that each event's fold follows from its identifier.
items.blocking: The use of a multivariate method is not declared, or the folds are not assigned by the event identifier.

items.question: Is every event evaluated by a model that did not train on it?
items.evidence: A declaration that no event is evaluated on its training fold.
items.blocking: Events are evaluated on their training folds, or the evaluation folds are not declared.

items.question: Is an overtraining check reported?
items.evidence: The result of the comparison between training and held-out response.
items.blocking: A multivariate method is used without an overtraining check.

items.question: Does every alternative-sample comparison use samples of the same process and the same simulation campaign?
items.evidence: Each comparison declares that its two samples match in process and in campaign.
items.blocking: The comparisons are not declared, or one compares samples of different processes or campaigns.

items.question: Does every uncertainty value taken from elsewhere name its source?
items.evidence: Each cited value names the source it is taken from.
items.blocking: The cited values are not declared, or one has no source.

items.question: Is the sensitivity compared with the previous analysis on the same signal points and the same luminosity?
items.evidence: The reference of the previous analysis and a comparison on the same signal points and luminosity, or a statement that no previous analysis exists.
items.blocking: The comparison is absent, or it uses different signal points or a different luminosity.

items.question: Does the note respect its page limit?
items.evidence: The page count of the built note and the page limit the request sets.
items.blocking: The page count is not reported, or it exceeds the stated limit.

items.question: Is every figure and table referenced from the text?
items.evidence: Each figure and table of the note is marked as referenced.
items.blocking: None; an unreferenced figure or table is an advisory finding.

items.question: Does the note build from its sources with one recorded command?
items.evidence: The build command and a record that it reproduced the note.
items.blocking: No build command is recorded, or the build did not reproduce the note.

items.question: Can a physicist outside the analysis follow the strategy, the background estimate and the result from the note alone?
items.evidence: Located passages the reviewer could not follow, or none.
items.blocking: None; readability findings are advisory.
